CIRCUIT: four parallel branches hung between a top rail (y~385, x 243..735) and a bottom rail (y~610, x 245..752), with the 4 Ohm resistor sitting IN the top rail (x 393..495) so the top rail is split into two distinct nodes. Left to right: I-DC3 (3A) rises at x~243; R4 (2 kOhm) at x~366; then R0 (4 Ohm) breaks the rail; then the series pair C1 (2F) over V-DC5 (20V) drops at x~562; then L2 (6 mH) at x~745. The GND symbol hangs below the bottom rail at x~569. Everything is inside a hand-drawn page border which is not a conductor and touches nothing.

NET MAP:
  0  = bottom rail y~610 x 245..752, plus the GND stub: bottom of I-DC3, bottom of R4, bottom of V-DC5, bottom of L2, GND6.
  n1 = top-LEFT node, y~385 from x~243 to x~393: top lead of I-DC3, top lead of R4 (joins at site S2), left lead of R0.
  n2 = top-RIGHT node, y~385 from x~495 to x~735 and down the right riser: right lead of R0, top lead of C1 (drops at site S0), top lead of L2.
  n3 = the short link between the two stacked parts of the middle branch, x~562, y 474..515: bottom lead of C1 to top lead of V-DC5. Two terminals, correct - the capacitor and the source are in series in that branch.

SITE DECISIONS (all four CRITICAL sites recorded explicitly; all are junctions):
  S0 (557,387) deg=3, dot=1.1, hop=0: plain tee - the top rail runs straight through left-right and a single stroke leaves it downward toward the capacitor; there is no ink above the rail at this x. A wire ending on another wire is a junction. The alternative would put C1's top lead on a one-terminal net and leave the whole C1/V-DC5 branch unfed.
  S2 (364,389) deg=3, dot=1.5, hop=0: identical geometry for R4's top lead dropping off the top rail. Junction; otherwise R4 would hang off a one-terminal node.
  S9 (567,613) deg=4, dot=1.6, hop=0: this is the only genuine four-way on the sheet. The vertical from V-DC5's bottom lead comes down, meets the bottom rail, and continues below into the GND symbol; the rail runs on both sides. inkmap at (567,613) shows continuous merged ink with no solder blob, no semicircular hop and no sideways jog - the vertical simply runs through the rail. Chosen: junction, i.e. the ground tap sits on the bottom rail. The crossing reading would separate the bottom rail (I-DC3, R4 and L2 returns) from the GND/V-DC5 node, which would leave the entire C1+V-DC5 branch unable to pass any current (no return path from n2 back to the rail) and would leave the circuit's only ground reference attached to just two terminals of a dead-end stub. Per the dataset's ink prior a plain crossing with no hop is a real junction, and the drafter clearly intended the conventional 'ground symbol on the bottom rail'; both arguments agree.
  S10 (371,614) deg=3, dot=1.1, hop=0: R4's bottom lead arrives from above and terminates on the bottom rail; inkmap shows the vertical stopping in the rail, not passing through it. Tee, junction. Otherwise R4's bottom would be a one-terminal net and the 2 kOhm would carry no current.
  Non-critical sites S5 (395,533), S7 (600,554) and S8 (609,561) are the handwritten '2 K Ohm' and '20V' labels brushing the R4 and V-DC5 boxes. Left at default; they change nothing.

PORT / PIN FIXES: none needed. Unusually for this dataset, every terminal the tracer picked already sits on a real lead - I checked all seven components in the _comps crop. The two 'unused port candidate' warnings, at (440,414) on R0 and (389,524) on R4, are the '4 Ohm' and '2 K' value text touching the boxes; neither is a lead, so both terminals stay where they are. No three-terminal parts on this sheet, so there is no pin order to get wrong, and no terminal was left null.

CLASSES: all seven symbols match - Resistor (zigzag, '4 Ohm'), Resistor (vertical zigzag, '2 K Ohm'), Capacitor (two parallel plates, '2F'), Inductor (vertical coil, '6 mH'), I-DC (circle with up arrow, '3A'), V-DC (circle with + over -, '20V'), GND. No re-classification.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. Final netlist is 7 components / 4 nets; every net has at least two terminals and the ground reference is a proper rail. This one agreed with the tracer's default answer end to end - the decisions file records that agreement explicitly rather than leaving the critical sites unstated.
